sentences.text: The present suit was instituted by the appellants in 1974 seeking permanent injunction as the respondents attempted to encroach on their property.
The suit schedule property was described as no. 44/6.
The respondents in their written statement claimed ownership and possession of property no. 42, acknowledging that other properties lay in between.
A feeble vague objection was raised, but not pursued, questioning the title of the appellants.

The respondents raised no genuine objection to the validity or genuineness of the government documents and the registered sale deeds produced by the appellants in support of their lawful possession of the suit property.
The original defendant no.1 did not appear in person to depose, and be crossexamined in the suit.
His younger brother deposed on the basis of a power of attorney, acknowledging that the latter had separated from his elder brother.
No explanation was furnished why the original defendant did not appear in person to depose.
